claims.claim: Qwen 3.x chat template rejects the reasoning_effort values vLLM's OpenAI API accepts: template allows only xhigh|medium|low and calls raise_exception on high/minimal/max, while vLLM's ChatCompletionRequest.reasoning_effort Literal is none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max and is forwarded verbatim into chat_template_kwargs.
claims.title: [Bug]: Cannot pass `xhigh` reasoning effort to vLLM provider
claims.fixed_in: NOT FIXED. No fix exists in vLLM as of the pinned 2026-08-10 build, and none upstream since. Verified directly in the pinned image: vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py:231-232 declares reasoning_effort as Literal['none','minimal','low','medium','high','xhigh','max'], and build_chat_params (same file, ~line 540) puts reasoning_effort=self.reasoning_effort into extra_kwargs unconditionally, which merge_kwargs folds into chat_template_kwargs. The shipped template declares reasoning_effort, so resolve_chat_template_kwargs does NOT filter it out, and the raise_exception fires.
claims.evidence: Reporter running 'Qwen3.8 27B model in vLLM' quotes the server response verbatim: 'Unexpected reasoning effort high. Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low.' after a client translated xhigh->high; 'medium and low work as expected'.

additional_issues.note: Downstream workaround: clamp the value client-side rather than fix the template.

additional_issues.note: Closed WITHOUT merge (merged=false, merged_at=null). Only the 'none' case was ever addressed; the equivalent mapping landed via PR #43401 (merged 2026-05-27, commit 52a31ccecca203effd490a5b496dc5f8d9496654), which is in the pinned build but only injects enable_thinking and still forwards the raw reasoning_effort string.

claims.claim: Tool-call arguments arriving as a JSON string from OpenAI-compatible clients blow up the Qwen template's tool_call.arguments|items with 'TypeError: Can only get item pairs from a mapping'.
claims.title: Qwen3.8 chat template crashes on OpenAI JSON-string tool arguments
claims.fixed_in: Template NOT fixed (issue open; filed against exactly our revision). BUT the failure is unreachable through vLLM's OpenAI server in the 2026-08-10 pinned build: vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py:1875-1915 (_postprocess_messages) json.loads() every assistant function.arguments string into a dict, coerces None/'' to {}, and drops empty tool_calls, before apply_chat_template runs. Called on both the sync and async render paths (chat_utils.py:1950 and :1989). This normalization long predates 2026-08-10.
claims.evidence: Issue body pins 'Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B revision 1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0 shipped chat_template.jinja', notes 'The template iterates tool_call.arguments|items ... OpenAI-compatible assistant history normally carries function.arguments as a serialized JSON string', and shows 'TypeError: Can only get item pairs from a mapping.'

claims.claim: The template emits an OPEN '<think>\n' in the generation prompt, and with --reasoning-parser qwen3 / qwen3_xml this leaks reasoning tags into content and leaves reasoning_content empty.

claims.fixed_in: Still open; filed 2026-08-10, the same day the pinned image was built, so no fix can be in it. However it does NOT apply to our flags: the reproducer runs with NO --reasoning-parser, and the reporter states --reasoning-parser qwen3 'works, and it is a usable workaround'. claims.claim: Prior-turn reasoning retained vs stripped (preserve_thinking / enable_thinking); empty <think></think> blocks injected into history; prefix/KV cache invalidation from mutated history.
claims.title: chat template emits empty historical <think> blocks, causing prompt drift and cache invalidation
claims.fixed_in:
NOT fixed in the template we ship. The requested one-line guard ('and reasoning_content') was never applied: sha256 c3cf9e34... still renders '<|im_start|>assistant
<think>
' + reasoning_content + '
</think>

' for EVERY historical assistant turn whenever preserve_thinking is undefined or true (the default), producing an empty <think>

</think> block when reasoning_content is absent - which is always the case for OpenAI clients that do not echo reasoning back. This is a template-side defect; no vLLM release can fix it, so the 2026-08-10 build is irrelevant to it.
claims.evidence: Issue states 'historical assistant turns can emit empty `<think>...</think>` blocks even when `reasoning_content` is empty ... these empty historical `<think>` blocks change the serialized prompt without adding any useful information', and proposes changing the guard to '{%- if loop.index0 > ns.last_query_index and reasoning_content %}'.

claims.claim: vLLM prefers chat_template.jinja over the chat_template key of tokenizer_config.json (or transformers v5 changed that precedence).
claims.fixed_in: N/A - nothing to fix. This is documented, intentional behavior, not a bug, and no issue exists in any of the five target repos.
claims.evidence: Grounded directly in the pinned image instead of an issue: transformers 5.15.0 tokenization_utils_base.py:1783 carries the comment 'If independent chat template file(s) exist, they take priority over template entries in the tokenizer config', reading chat_template.jinja into chat_templates['default'] (lines 1785-1799), and save_chat_templates (line 3305-3306) pops 'chat_template' from tokenizer_config 'To ensure it doesn't somehow end up in the config too'. vLLM's resolve_chat_template (vllm/renderers/hf.py:262-300) never reads either file itself: priority is (1) explicit --chat-template, (2) AutoProcessor template but ONLY when tools is None, (3) tokenizer.get_chat_template(), (4) predefined fallbacks. Because we serve with --enable-auto-tool-choice, tools is not None, so step 2 is skipped and the tokenizer template is authoritative.

claims.divergence_check: No divergence risk in our repos: for Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, malaiwah/Qwen3.8-27B-K4 and Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B the chat_template.jinja bytes and the tokenizer_config.json 'chat_template' string hash IDENTICALLY (c3cf9e34abf4f9e3... and e84f32a23fdda276... respectively). Whichever source wins, the rendered prompt is the same.

claims.evidence: The merge commit's diff to vllm/renderers/hf.py adds exactly '+def _detect_developer_role_support', '+def _convert_developer_to_system', '+def _consolidate_system_messages' and the two call sites; the PR touched only vllm/renderers/hf.py (+69/-1) and tests/renderers/test_hf.py (+322).

A conversation with two plain 'system' messages never reaches _consolidate_system_messages and still hits the template's raise_exception.

official_template_history.method: GET https://huggingface.co/api/models/<repo>/commits/main?limit=100 (authenticated with /var/tmp/hf-home-3/token), then for EVERY commit sha GET https://huggingface.co/<repo>/resolve/<sha>/chat_template.jinja and sha256 the bytes. A commit 'touched the template' iff its blob hash differs from its parent's. This is stronger than reading commit titles, which do not list changed files.
